title: Core Web Vitals: LCP, INP and CLS
description: Learn about Core Web Vitals: LCP, INP and CLS. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Core Web Vitals are the essential metrics for measuring user experience on the web. They represent the key aspects of web performance that directly impact how users perceive your site's speed, responsiveness, and visual stability.

Core Web Vitals consist of three specific metrics that Google uses to evaluate user experience: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). These metrics help you understand and improve the real-world user experience of your website.

LCP measures loading performance. It reports the render time of the largest content element visible in the viewport, such as an image, video, or large text block. A good LCP score is under 2.5 seconds.

data.title: Measuring LCP
data.content: Use the Web Vitals API to measure LCP in production.

data.text: INP measures responsiveness. It assesses the time from when a user first interacts with your page to when the browser can respond to that interaction. A good INP score is under 200 milliseconds.

data.title: Measuring INP

data.text: CLS measures visual stability. It quantifies how much the page content shifts unexpectedly during loading. A good CLS score is under 0.1. This prevents users from accidentally clicking the wrong button when content moves.

data.title: Measuring CLS
data.content: Track layout shifts to improve visual stability.

items: Optimize and compress images (use WebP, AVIF formats)
Preload important resources (critical CSS, fonts, hero images)
Use server-side rendering or static generation for initial content
Use CDN for faster content delivery
Minimize JavaScript execution time (code splitting, lazy loading)
Use web workers for CPU-intensive tasks
Avoid long tasks that block the main thread
Reserve space for dynamic content (use CSS aspect-ratio)
Avoid inserting content above existing content
Use transform animations instead of layout-changing properties
Ensure images have explicit width and height attributes
Preload fonts to prevent font swap layout shifts

data.title: Field Data vs Lab Data
data.text: Core Web Vitals are based on real-user field data from Chrome, not lab data from tools like Lighthouse. While lab data is useful for debugging, field data represents actual user experience.
Set up continuous monitoring of Core Web Vitals in production to catch performance regressions early. Use tools like Google Search Console, PageSpeed Insights, or custom analytics implementations.

data.content: Set up all three Core Web Vitals monitoring.

terms.definition: Measures loading performance by tracking when the largest content element appears in the viewport.
Measures responsiveness by tracking the time from user interaction to visual response.
Measures visual stability by quantifying unexpected layout shifts during page load.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Core Web Vitals measure real user experience: LCP (loading), INP (responsiveness), CLS (stability)
Monitor these metrics in production using the Web Vitals API
Optimize images and critical resources for better LCP
Reduce main thread blocking for better INP
Reserve space for content to prevent CLS
data.takeaway: Core Web Vitals provide a unified framework for measuring and improving user experience across all web applications.
